did_you_know.text: Did you know? The bronze altar was exceptionally large: it was twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and ten cubits high.
Did you know? The Sea was a round vessel ten cubits in diameter and five cubits high; the text says that a line thirty cubits long encircled it.
Did you know? The Sea stood on twelve oxen: three faced north, three west, three south, and three east, with their backs turned inward.
Did you know? The rim of the Sea was a handbreadth thick and shaped like the rim of a cup, decorated with a lily-blossom design; it held three thousand baths.
Did you know? There were ten basins beside the Sea, five on the right and five on the left, for washing the parts of the burnt offerings; the Sea itself was used by the priests for washing.
Did you know? Solomon made ten gold lampstands according to a prescribed design and placed five on the right and five on the left in the temple.
Did you know? The temple had ten tables, five on each side, as well as one hundred gold bowls.
Did you know? Huram’s work included not only bronze utensils but also two pillars, capitals, grilles, and pomegranates that decorated the tops of the pillars.
Did you know? The bronze objects were cast in the Jordan Valley, in the ground between Succoth and Zeredathah.
Did you know? Among the gold objects made for the house of God were the gold altar, the tables for the bread of the Presence, and the lampstands with their lamps.
